title: Chapter 11: Accident Procedures & Good Samaritan Law

blocks.content: What to Do If You Are in an Accident

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Immediate actions after an accident involve stopping safely, calling emergency services (112/108), and rendering first aid if trained.
Spinal injury victims should never be moved unless there is an immediate risk of fire or explosion.
Section 134A of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019 grants comprehensive legal protection to Good Samaritans.
Good Samaritans render voluntary assistance and cannot be forced to provide personal details or pay for hospital admissions.
112 serves as the unified Single Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) across India.

blocks.content: Do NOT move victims with spinal injuries unless fire/explosion risk.

items: Stop the vehicle immediately at a safe place
Check if anyone is injured — do not move seriously injured persons unless there is danger of fire
Call emergency services: Police — 100, Ambulance — 108
Provide first aid if you are trained to do so
Do not flee the scene — leaving the scene of an accident is an offence
Inform the nearest police station
Note down details: time, place, other vehicle number, witnesses
Do not move the vehicles before police arrive (unless blocking emergency traffic)
Cooperate with police and give a true account of what happened

blocks.content: A Good Samaritan is a person who voluntarily helps an accident victim without any expectation of reward.

items: A Good Samaritan CANNOT be harassed, detained, or coerced by the police
They are entitled to confidentiality of their personal information
They are NOT legally liable for any harm that may result from their help
They are NOT required to stay at the accident scene after helping
They may be asked to give information as a witness, but cannot be forced to do so
The law encourages citizens to call ambulance and police and provide basic first aid
Remember that Section 134A of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019 specifically governs Good Samaritan protections.
112 is designated as the Single Emergency Response Support System (ERSS).
Moving a victim with spinal injuries is strictly prohibited unless there is a fire/explosion risk.
